title: Policy on Trading in Healius Securities

tiers.name: all Healius employees and Directors
tiers.description: All employees and Directors of Healius. Subject to the general insider trading prohibition in Clause 3 (no dealing while in possession of price-sensitive information) regardless of trading window, exemption or clearance.

tiers.name: Prohibited Person
tiers.description: A Director, the Controlled Entity of a Director, a KMP, the Company Secretary, or the Controlled Entity of a KMP or Company Secretary. Confined to dealing within trading windows unless prior written clearance under Clause 6.2 or an automatic exemption under Clause 6.3 applies; also bound by the Clause 6.5 hedging ban.

tiers.name: Director (other than Chair) or Company Secretary
tiers.description: A Director other than the Chair, or the Company Secretary, or the Controlled Entity of either; a Prohibited Person whose closed-period clearance decision-maker is the Chair (or the Audit Committee Chair if the Chair is unavailable).

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Healius Board, or their Controlled Entity; a Prohibited Person whose closed-period clearance decision-maker is the Audit Committee Chair (or the Managing Director if unavailable).

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Key Management Personnel other than Directors, per AASB 124, or their Controlled Entity; a Prohibited Person whose closed-period clearance decision-maker is any of the Chair, the Managing Director, or the Company Secretary.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Either the Managing Director or the Directors may at any time partly or wholly restrict an otherwise open trading window (having regard to Listing Rule 3.1A matters and confidentiality risk), converting it into a closed period in which Clause 6.2 exceptional-circumstances clearance is required; confidentiality of such a restriction is not addressed.

rules.detail: Derivatives are not named as a standalone activity. Healius Securities include 'derivatives or any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market', so an exchange-traded derivative is a Healius Security and dealing in it is confined to trading windows or prior written clearance.
rules.evidence: any other securities of Healius including debentures, options, rights, derivatives or any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: The definition of Healius Securities requires derivatives/financial products to be 'able to be traded on a financial market'. A bespoke bilateral OTC put and call with a bank is arguably not itself tradeable on a market, so it is unclear whether it is a Healius Security at all for the purposes of the trading-window and clearance regime; the general insider trading prohibition in Clause 3 would still apply regardless of instrument.
Absolute ban on hedging or any other arrangement limiting the economic risk of any Healius Securities, with no distinction between vested and unvested holdings and no exemption route referenced.
rules.evidence: Prohibited Persons must not enter into a hedging arrangement, or enter into any other arrangement which limits the economic risk related to any Healius Securities.

rules.detail: Clause 6.5 hedging prohibition applies only to Prohibited Persons; hedging by other employees is not otherwise addressed beyond the general insider trading prohibition.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar arrangement falls within the broad 'deal' definition (disposing of, entering into an agreement to trade, or taking part in any transaction associated with Healius Securities) and so is confined to trading windows or prior clearance.
rules.evidence: “deal” is a broad concept and includes (whether as principal or agent) acquiring, disposing of, or subscribing for, any type of Healius Securities, transferring beneficial ownership, trading (either directly or indirectly), entering into an agreement to trade and includes taking part in any transaction associated with such things.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named. It would fall within the broad 'deal' definition ('disposing of ... any transaction associated with such things') and so is confined to trading windows or prior clearance, though the Policy does not address the mechanics of short positions or borrowed stock.
rules.evidence: “deal” is a broad concept and includes (whether as principal or agent) acquiring, disposing of, or subscribing for, any type of Healius Securities

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not encompassed by the 'deal' definition.

CFDs are not named. A CFD would be a 'financial product' within the Healius Securities definition if regarded as 'able to be traded on a financial market', so dealing in one would be confined to trading windows or prior clearance.
rules.evidence: any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly contemplated as an example of secured lending; a secured lender's on-market disposal of the shares in exercise of its rights is automatically exempt from the closed-period prohibition (no clearance needed). Entering the margin loan itself is not captured by the 'deal' definition (which does not mention encumbrance), so creating the loan is not restricted by the trading-window regime.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Healius Securities on-market that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Granting security over Healius Securities is not named and is not included in the 'deal' definition, so it is not itself a Dealing subject to trading windows or clearance. The automatic exemption for a secured lender's forced on-market sale (6.3(j)) implicitly assumes Prohibited Persons may grant security over their shares.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Healius Securities on-market that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Not limited to margin loans: the exemption covers 'a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement', so other secured financing (e.g. a bank loan secured on the collared shares) is implicitly within scope, and a resulting on-market forced sale is automatically exempt from the closed-period ban.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Healius Securities on-market that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: No minimum holding period or short-term dealing restriction is stated; the only timing constraint is the trading window / closed period regime.

financing_disclosure: Director; trigger: any change in notifiable interests (including from a secured lender's forced on-market sale); to whom: Company Secretary, for ASX Appendix 3Y filing; deadline: 5 business days of the change

exemption_authority: The Board does not have power to exempt anyone from insider trading law (Clause 6.2). Closed-period clearance is limited to defined 'exceptional circumstances' (severe financial hardship; a pressing financial commitment satisfiable only by selling; an arm's-length party exercising contractual rights to require a purchase/sale; or any other circumstance the designated decision-maker deems exceptional) decided by the Chair, Audit Committee Chair, Managing Director or Company Secretary depending on tier.

bespoke_clauses.clause: “Healius Securities” means the following types of securities: ... any other securities of Healius including debentures, options, rights, derivatives or any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a bespoke bilateral OTC put and call with a bank is not itself 'able to be traded on a financial market', it may fall outside the definition of Healius Securities altogether, which would place the collar's derivative legs outside the trading-window and clearance regime (though the general insider trading prohibition in Clause 3 still applies to the underlying shares).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Prohibited Persons must not enter into a hedging arrangement, or enter into any other arrangement which limits the economic risk related to any Healius Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The purchased put and written call that form the collar are squarely an arrangement limiting economic risk in Healius Securities and are expressly and absolutely banned for every Prohibited Person, with no vesting-state carve-out and no clearance or exemption route, which is a threshold obstacle independent of how the loan is structured.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Healius Securities on-market that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's on-market enforcement sale of the collared shares following a loan default is automatically exempt from the closed-period prohibition, so the bank's enforcement rights are not blocked by trading windows even if the executive is otherwise restricted at the time of enforcement.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exceptional circumstances gate for closed-period clearance
bespoke_clauses.clause: “exceptional circumstances” are: (i) severe financial hardship; (ii) a pressing financial commitment that cannot reasonably be satisfied otherwise than by selling the Healius Securities; (iii) an arm's-length party exercising contractual rights to require the Prohibited Person to buy or sell; or (iv) any other circumstances the designated decision-maker deems exceptional.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside an open trading window, discretionary collar or loan entry is not automatically clearable; it would need to be brought within one of these narrow exceptional-circumstances categories (or a decision-maker's residual discretion) or else wait for the next open window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Either the Managing Director of Healius or the Directors may at any time partly or wholly restrict the trading windows in paragraphs A-E inclusive of Clause 6.1, during which restrictions all of the provisions of Clause 6.2 of this document apply despite the fact that a trading window is open.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar entry timed for an open trading window can be abruptly converted into a closed period at the discretion of the Managing Director or the Board, adding execution timing risk.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no liability / no representation on clearance
bespoke_clauses.clause: The terms of this Policy, and actions taken by any person under or in reliance on it, including dealing ... on the basis of a prior written clearance ... do not constitute a representation or approval by or on behalf of Healius about the legality or appropriateness of the relevant dealing and Healius is not liable to the person so dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Obtaining trading-window clearance for the collar does not immunise the executive (or the bank as counterparty) from underlying insider trading liability, which Healius expressly disclaims responsibility for.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Directors require that in interpreting the terms of this Policy ... Prohibited Persons and designated decision-makers follow the rules of interpretation in ASX Listing Rule 19.2, namely: ... by looking beyond form to substance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any argument that the OTC collar is not 'hedging' in form is unlikely to succeed given the express substance-over-form interpretive mandate, reinforcing that Clause 6.5 will be read to catch the collar's economic effect.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (c) transfers of Healius Securities from a Prohibited Person to an (d) an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clause 6.3(c) is incomplete/truncated in the version of the policy lodged with ASX, leaving its scope unknowable; it should not be relied on as an exemption for the collar structure without clarification from the Company Secretary.

summary: A funded collar is not available under this policy because Clause 6.5 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on Prohibited Persons (Directors, KMP, the Company Secretary and their Controlled Entities) entering any hedging arrangement or other arrangement that limits the economic risk of Healius Securities, with no vesting-state carve-out, no clearance path and no exemption. This threshold prohibition applies regardless of whether the OTC put and call would otherwise be treated as 'dealing' in a 'Healius Security' (itself doubtful, since that definition requires derivatives to be 'able to be traded on a financial market', arguably excluding a bespoke bilateral bank product). The loan leg is comparatively unproblematic: granting security over the shares is not captured by the 'deal' definition, and a secured lender's (the bank's) eventual on-market enforcement sale is automatically exempt from the closed-period restriction, so the financing structure alone would not be blocked. Because the hedging ban is a standalone, absolute prohibition rather than a clearance condition, restructuring timing, tiers or documentation cannot cure it; the collar would need to be abandoned or replaced with an unhedged facility if this policy is to be complied with.
